discovery: Development of controlled/living radical polymerization (ATRP and RAFT), which enables precise synthesis of polymers with tailored architectures
rationale: Recent Chemistry prizes went to molecular biology and computation (2024) and to framework materials (2025), so the committee may turn to synthetic and polymer chemistry next. Controlled radical polymerization has a huge citation footprint and wide industrial use in coatings, biomaterials and electronics, and it has long been a frontrunner backed by Wolf Prize and Citation Laureate recognition. Its main inventors (ATRP by Matyjaszewski and Sawamoto, RAFT by Rizzardo) form a natural trio.
